items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Do you remember when you first met Charlie Parker? [INTERVIEWEE] When we were working at Wehnwood Beach we'd go by where he was playing...

ctx.x: Oh, yes. In other words, that was the era of the well-trained musician, that was the last of the well-trained musicians. Out of that era came Charlie Parker, Dizzy, and the bop era. These musicians, we never went out against each other, say, I'm going to outplay another pianist. We had some terrific women around. We'd just exchange ideas and play and have a ball and drink and eat together, but we never had that thing that someone's going to cut you completely out or make a fool out of you.
You mentioned other women. Who were some of the other women?
